# A `:value` binding on radio writes back the option that was clicked. The
# override says so itself -- `onClick=func() { change({value = opt}) }` -- and
# the binding pass has to take the value from that emit.
#
# It invented a parameter on the callback instead. Compose's onClick is
# `() -> Unit`, so the emitted Kotlin did not compile, and `opt` -- the whole
# point of the loop -- never reached the write-back. Both directions are
# checked: the injection used to stop at the first match it walked into, which
# for this override's if/else is the branch that is not taken.

sngl generate --lang kotlin --platform android --out h horizontal.sngl
grep 'onClick = \{' h/MainScreen.kt
grep 'pick = "a"' h/MainScreen.kt
grep 'pick = "b"' h/MainScreen.kt
! grep 'newValue ->' h/MainScreen.kt
! grep 'onClick = \{\}' h/MainScreen.kt

sngl generate --lang kotlin --platform android --out v vertical.sngl
grep 'pick = "a"' v/MainScreen.kt
grep 'pick = "b"' v/MainScreen.kt
! grep 'newValue ->' v/MainScreen.kt
! grep 'onClick = \{\}' v/MainScreen.kt

-- horizontal.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"

component main {
    var pick string = "a"
    radio(:value=pick, options=["a", "b"], direction="horizontal")
    text(value=pick)
}
-- vertical.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"

component main {
    var pick string = "a"
    radio(:value=pick, options=["a", "b"])
    text(value=pick)
}
